title: The key must trace to the source
statement: Every claim in a keyed answer must trace to something the source says, but naming the category of what it describes is not an error.
detail: For argument-conclusion items, an audit maps each claim in the correct option to a point the passage makes, and a correct option with an unmapped claim fails factual accuracy; appeals to synthesis don't rescue a genuine shift of domain, but naming the category of what the passage described is the skill the standard asks for (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/src/inceptbench/prompts/question/ela_evaluation.txt`). The audit was narrowed after it over-flagged exactly those category-label summaries and failed good concluding-statement items (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/tests/test_evaluator_prompt_rules_411_418.py`).
against: The audit is written for argument conclusions, and applied strictly it misfired on legitimate synthesis until it was narrowed (`icloud-work/inceptbench-main/tests/test_evaluator_prompt_rules_411_418.py`, lines 17-19).

evidence.quote: - ANY correct option with a `NONE` claim → `factual_accuracy = 0.0`. "Pedagogical synthesis" / "appropriate inference for hard items" do NOT rescue genuine domain shifts. They DO rescue category-label synthesis covered by the bullet above — that is the standard's intended skill, not a violation.
concluding-statement items were failing on `factual_accuracy` because Audit B was over-flagging the exact category-label synthesis the standard expects.
True-but-unsupported is wrong; the correct answer must have a citeable evidence line (inference-overreach trap).
